page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Perforins
steps.why: The name says it: they perforate the membrane of the infected cell.
common_mistakes: Saying perforins destroy proteins. Granzymes do that.
Placing perforins inside the cell. They act on the membrane.
steps.memory_tip: Perforins perforate: they make the pores.
steps.margin_note: Two rows, in the order they act.
lines: Perforins form pores in the cell membrane
They make the cell burst by letting fluid

steps.label: Granzymes
steps.why: Once a pore exists the enzymes can reach inside and switch on the cell's own self-destruction.
common_mistakes: Leaving out that they enter through the pores.
steps.memory_tip: Granzymes are enzymes that go in through the pores.
steps.margin_note: Say they enter through the pores perforins made.
lines: Granzymes enter the infected cell through

lines.text: They activate proteins that destroy the cell

insider_note: They work in order: perforins make the hole, granzymes go through it. Say so, and the difference is clear.
